improvements: Consider a larger display or a crop on the village earthworks so house plots read more clearly at thumbnail size.
Mention that the blue strip is a canal or watercourse, so readers do not mistake it for part of the village.
grade.reason: The lidar image clearly shows the abandoned village earthworks and the surrounding ridge-and-furrow strips, which directly support the paragraph on conversion to pasture. It complements the Wharram Percy photograph rather than repeating it. Fine house-plot detail softens at small size.

figure.learningGoal: Shows how a deserted village survives only as earthworks, with ridge and furrow field patterns still visible around it.
figure.caption: Lidar image of the deserted medieval village at Wormleighton, Warwickshire, showing village earthworks and surrounding ridge and furrow.
figure.alt: Shaded lidar terrain image of fields near Wormleighton. The faint outlines of former village earthworks sit among parallel strips of ridge and furrow.
